notice: Teaching designs with synthetic examples. No documents, prompts or credentials are sent to a model. A design record is not a production approval.

examples.label: Document intelligence
examples.title: From a document to a checked business record.
examples.goal: Prepare a checked invoice draft and its evidence for an accounts-payable reviewer.
examples.baseline: Compare against manual entry plus OCR and deterministic validation on the same documents. Count accepted records, corrections and reviewer minutes, including exceptions.
examples.why: Ingest, extract, validate and stage are known steps. Add an agent only if resolving exceptions requires choosing among permitted tools. A fixed workflow can contain several model calls.
examples.boundary: One tenant, an approved document collection and a staging ledger. Read purchase orders and vendor records. Never issue a payment, change bank details or approve your own output.
examples.sources: Invoice INV-DEMO-104, page 1; purchase order PO-DEMO-28; current invoice policy with owner, version and review date. All records in this lesson are synthetic.
examples.ingestion: Quarantine and scan uploads; validate file type and size; classify the document; extract fields and table structure with page coordinates. Preserve the original and its content hash under the retention policy.
examples.grounding: Check required fields, duplicate invoice keys, totals, currency and purchase-order references in code. Retrieve only permitted policy passages. Treat document text as evidence, never as a new instruction or permission.
examples.quality: Measure field exact-match and document-level acceptance on held-out vendors, layouts, scans and languages. Calibrate review thresholds against observed field errors. Extraction confidence is not proof that an invoice is legitimate.
examples.readOutcome: Checked draft returned with page references. No business record was written.
examples.writeOutcome: Synthetic staging receipt received. Draft stored for the AP process; no payment was issued.
examples.evidenceDetail: Read the permitted invoice. Extract its fields, reconcile totals against the purchase order and attach page references.
examples.proposalDetail: Build a typed draft with source references and validation results. The model can propose fields; application checks decide whether the draft can continue.
examples.review: The AP reviewer sees the source pages, field differences, validation results, target record and exact proposed arguments. Approval binds to this payload and expires if it changes.
examples.bounded: Only stage a validated draft inside the approved tenant and collection. All required checks must pass. Payment and vendor-master changes remain unavailable.
examples.failure: A scan hides part of the invoice total. The field is unresolved, so the draft goes to review instead of inventing a value.
examples.operation: Watch correction rate by field and vendor, exception queue age, duplicate prevention, extraction drift, receipt reconciliation and total cost per accepted record.
examples.improvement: Label adjudicated extraction errors and train a new custom document model when justified. Hold out unseen layouts and suppliers. Rebuild the index for policy changes. These are separate changes from fine-tuning a language model.
acceptance: Hold for correction; preserve the original page and missing-field reason.
Reject the duplicate staging key; do not create a second record.
No payment capability exists; deny the attempted tool and record the event.
Reconcile by idempotency key before retrying; report unknown until verified.

examples.label: Internal knowledge assistant
examples.title: An answer that stays inside the employee's access.
examples.goal: Answer an employee's IT-policy question with current, accessible evidence, or explain why it cannot be answered.
examples.owner: Internal service owner and knowledge owners
examples.baseline: Compare search plus the existing help desk against grounded answers on the same questions. Measure supported answers, correct abstention, user resolution and total service cost.
examples.why: A chat interface does not require an autonomous agent. Start with authorized retrieval and a cited answer. Add narrowly scoped actions, such as creating an access-request ticket, only as a separate capability.
examples.boundary: Verify employee and tenant identity. Filter every retrieval by current access before content reaches the model. No payroll lookup, cross-user memory, entitlement changes or access grants.
examples.sources: IT-POLICY-DEMO, section 3; owner: IT service desk; approved version: v3. Restricted documents and their titles stay out of the answer. The policy is synthetic.
examples.ingestion: Register source owners, approved versions, review dates, sensitivity and access metadata. Chunk with document and section references. Propagate edits, deletions and permission changes to the index and caches.
examples.grounding: Derive user and group scope on the server, not from a prompt. Retrieve only authorized passages. If evidence is absent, conflicting or stale, abstain and route to the owner. Re-check access on follow-up turns and before writes.
examples.quality: Measure claim support, citation correctness, authorized retrieval recall and correct abstention. Test employee roles, revoked groups, follow-up questions, stale policies and adversarial documents. A plausible answer can still fail.
examples.readOutcome: Cited policy answer returned from permitted evidence. No ticket or entitlement was created.
examples.writeOutcome: Synthetic service-desk receipt received. A request ticket exists; access has not been granted.
examples.evidenceDetail: Use verified tenant and group scope to select the current policy before any passage reaches the model. Restricted results are excluded.
examples.proposalDetail: Return supported claims and citations. When action is enabled, draft a ticket containing only the required fields, bound to the current employee.
examples.review: The employee reviews the ticket category and data being shared. The service owner approves the action policy. Creating a request never grants the requested entitlement.
examples.bounded: Create a request ticket for the signed-in employee in allowlisted categories, with consent, rate limits and a deduplication key. Never grant access or alter group membership.
examples.failure: The relevant policy is missing or stale. The assistant says it cannot establish the answer and directs the employee to the knowledge owner.
examples.operation: Watch unsupported-claim and abstention rates, permission failures, source age, unresolved questions, latency, ticket duplicates and cost per verified resolution.
examples.improvement: Fix source content or retrieval when evidence is wrong or missing. Adjust prompts for recurring response errors. Use reviewed feedback for evaluation cases; conversations do not automatically become training data.
acceptance: Exclude it before model context; do not reveal its title or existence.
Abstain and name the supported escalation route.
Re-check authorization; refuse the write despite earlier approval.
Offer the request process; the grant operation is not an available tool.

sources.title: Anthropic: Building effective agents
sources.claim: Distinguishes predefined workflows from model-directed agents; complexity should be earned by the task.

sources.title: Anthropic: Demystifying evals for AI agents
sources.claim: Evaluate environment outcomes and combine code, model and human graders; model graders need calibration.

sources.title: Microsoft: Document Intelligence accuracy and confidence
sources.claim: Field confidence and extraction accuracy need interpretation and representative evaluation; custom document training is distinct from LLM training.

sources.title: Microsoft: Azure AI Search security filter pattern
sources.claim: Application-supplied principal filters trim retrieval. String filters are not independently an authentication mechanism.

sources.title: Microsoft: Claude models in Foundry
sources.claim: Hosting options, model availability and lifecycle vary. Configure applicable content safety during inference; do not assume deployment-time filtering.

sources.title: Microsoft: Data processing for Claude in Foundry
sources.claim: Azure-hosted and Anthropic-hosted options have distinct processing boundaries. Anthropic is the seller and operator for both.

sources.title: Microsoft: Application tracing with OpenTelemetry
sources.claim: Foundry tracing can store OpenTelemetry traces in Application Insights. Instrument application checks as well as model calls.
